title: Reliance on chance variation and natural selection stalls inquiry into physical causes

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Reliance on chance variation and natural selection stalls inquiry into physical causes

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: As long as fortuitous variation and the survival of the fittest are accepted as sufficient explanations in biology, they will tend to hold back careful investigation of the real physical causes of organic form.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: So long and so far as “fortuitous variation” and the “survival of the fittest” remain engrained as fundamental and satisfactory hypotheses in the philosophy of biology, so long will these “satisfactory and specious causes” tend to stay “severe and diligent inquiry,”

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter I, “Introductory”; topic “Mechanism versus final causes”. Scope: explanations of organic form in biology generally

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch01-01: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.19

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Bibliometric proxies are possible, but they substantially reinterpret the claim and cannot identify the proposed inhibition. Publication corpora also cover only part of biology and do not distinguish intellectual causation from changing methods or funding.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: One could code historical biological publications for reliance on selection language and for subsequent physical-mechanistic investigation, but neither category supplies a non-arbitrary measure of inquiry being held back.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Key terms such as sufficient explanation and real cause are normative.

The counterfactual amount of inquiry without the hypotheses is unobservable.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is a claim about the philosophy of biological explanation. Bibliometric proxies for research effort exist, but they do not contain the causal notion of a satisfactory hypothesis holding inquiry back, and any historical pattern is compatible with several stories about why morphologists chose the problems they did. The claim therefore has no measurable consequence that separates it from its rivals.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: A test would need a measure of how far selection is treated as a sufficient explanation and a measure of effort spent on physical causes of form, plus a result showing that the first suppresses the second. The claim does not fix either variable or a confirming threshold.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Publication counts cannot show that inquiry was stayed rather than redirected.

The claim is about the effect of accepting an explanation, not about a biological measurement.
